metadata.note: The Manassas Gap Rail Road, Manassas Junction - Gainesville - The Plains - Piedmont (Delaplane) - Markham - Front Royal - Strasburg - Woodstock - Mount Jackson, 87 mi, VA. Chartered 9 Mar 1850, opened in stages 1852-1859, ran its own public passenger and freight trains to 1861 (last confirmed year), was wrecked in the war, and transferred its property to the Orange and Alexandria in 1867. Drawn as five features, one per opening stage with its own proven start year, all ending 1861. Research report: research/branches/manassas_gap_railroad.txt.
sources: https://www.loc.gov/collections/chronicling-america/ -- Alexandria Gazette (sn85025007) MGRR advertisements 1851-1867, page OCR via loc.gov

https://www.nps.gov/places/information-panel-unfinished-railroad.htm -- NPS marker (Independent Line, trackage over the O&A)

metadata.operator_split: None drawn. 1852-1861 Manassas Gap RR ran its own trains (the 1861 Confederate period is not a split). 1862-1864 USMRR military-only - not drawn (Rule 1). Spring 1867 Manassas Gap RR briefly again (block [9]); from about June 1867 the Orange and Alexandria / Orange, Alexandria and Manassas - a real operator change; any successor feature belongs to the O&A row in its colour.
omitted: Block [9] Manassas Junction - Piedmont, spring 1867 (MGRR tri-weekly mixed train, about April/May - mid-June 1867, before the O&A took possession; Alexandria Gazette 1867-04-22 p3, 1867-05-23 p1, 1867-06-08 p1, 1867-09-11 p1, 1867-11-21 p2). Drawable only as an 1867 [ANCHOR]; per the report's recommendation it is left to the Orange and Alexandria / OA&M feature for this track, to start in 1867 with this interlude in its note, so the map does not carry two features for the same year.

Block [10] Alexandria - Manassas Junction through running over Orange and Alexandria track, 1852-1861: drawable NONE as a Manassas Gap feature (O&A track; MGRR's own through trains 1852 - about 1857 rest only on ad wording, and from about 1858 MGRR passengers rode the O&A's train). Leave to the O&A row.
USMRR military operation 1862-1864 (Rule 1: supply and troop trains only).
Never-railed: the Independent Line Gainesville - Alexandria, the Loudoun Branch, and Mount Jackson - Harrisonburg under the MGRR (completed by the O&A/OA&M in 1868).
Front Royal town spur (dates and passenger use unestablished).

not_yet_sourced: End of pre-war public service: last confirmed 1861 (June-August 1861 ads); no dated last public train before the March 1862 Confederate withdrawal.
Markham - Front Royal start: bracket 1853-1854 (Linden 1853 is secondary and not a passenger date); drawn from 1854.
Who ran the trains Alexandria - Manassas (MGRR through trains vs O&A trains) and the changeover date (about 1857-58); the O&A annual reports 1856-58 would settle it. Not drawn here either way.
headway_min year by year: one train a day each way is read from the 1852, 1853, 1857, 1859 and 1861 notices only.
Whether the surviving ex-Southern alignment differs anywhere from the 1852-1861 alignment.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 33.9 mi against 34 mi documented (Manassas Junction 0 - Gainesville 8 - Thoroughfare 14 - Broad Run 17 - The Plains 20 - Salem (Marshall) ~25 - Rectortown 30 - Piedmont (Delaplane) 34; Wikipedia station table after Black and Johnston, agreeing with the USMRR final report's Piedmont 34 / Front Royal 51 / Strasburg 61). Entirely on OSM rail tagged old_railway_operator=Southern apart from about 0.4 mi of untagged connecting track at Manassas. No straight-line legs. Whole line Manassas Junction - Mount Jackson traced 86.4 mi against 87 mi documented; every station waypoint lies within 0.0-1.6 km of the line (Front Royal 1.4 km, Buckton 1.6 km - town centroids, the line passed about a mile from Front Royal). Traced mileposts from Manassas vs documented: Gainesville 9.1/8, Broad Run 14.7/17, The Plains 19.8/20, Marshall 24.2/~25, Rectortown 30.0/30, Piedmont 33.9/34, Markham 38.6/38, Linden 42.8/43, Front Royal 50.0/51, Buckton 54.7/56, Strasburg 62.1/61, Toms Brook 68.0/68, Woodstock 73.8/75, Edinburg 79.4/81, Mount Jackson 86.4/87 - so a section's own figure can differ by 1-2 mi from the documented one (Strasburg - Woodstock 11.9 vs 14) because the cut is placed at the projection of the town-centre geocode, not at the old depot. Sections cut at the projection of the station point onto the trace, so the five features share endpoints and do not overlap. LATER ALIGNMENT: this is the surviving ex-Southern Railway / Norfolk Southern alignment (the Southern 'Manassas Branch', NS B-Line, live Manassas - Front Royal - Riverton - Strasburg Junction; railway=disused from about Strasburg Junction to near Mount Jackson, out of service since about 2013-2016; the last mile into Mount Jackson is NS track OSM names 'Chesapeake Western'). The line was wrecked and its rails lifted in 1862-1864 and rebuilt by the O&A/OA&M in 1867-68 and later owners; whether any curve, bridge approach (e.g. the Shenandoah River crossings near Riverton/Front Royal, rebuilt 1867) or station track was relocated between 1861 and today was NOT checked, so the 1852-1861 drawn years may sit on a later alignment in places. Not traced onto the N&W Hagerstown District that crosses at Riverton (trace stays on B-Line-named ways there) nor onto any B&O line at Strasburg (none in the routed path).

segments.note: Manassas Gap Rail Road's own passenger and freight trains, opened in three stages all in 1852: Manassas Junction - Turnpike Station (Gainesville) from 19 Jan 1852 ('On and after the 19th day of January, the FREIGHT AND PASSENGER TRAINS will run daily, (Sundays excepted,) between the Turnpike Station and Alexandria. Fare through, $1 45.' - Alexandria Gazette 17 Jan 1852 p2; rails still being laid Nov 1851, so no 1851 service; an O&A train may have reached Gainesville from 13 Jan 1852); to Salem (now Marshall) by 22 Jul 1852, the completion festival (Gazette 20 Jul 1852 p3; The Plains reached earlier in 1852 per civilwarintheeast); and to Piedmont Station (now Delaplane) by Oct 1852 ('now running daily ... between Alexandria and Piedmont Station, 61 miles from Alexandria', ad signed oct 12, Gazette 14 Dec 1852 p1). Trains ran through to Alexandria over the Orange and Alexandria's track (not drawn here; see metadata). Stage connections at The Plains for Middleburg and at Piedmont for Winchester via Paris and Millwood. headway_min 1440 = one train a day each way (Sundays excepted), read from the company's printed notices and timetables; the 1852-1861 frequency was not checked year by year, so treat it as an estimate outside the cited years. End 1861 is the last year with positive evidence: a Virginia Central RR timetable ad dated 3 Jun 1861 (Richmond Daily Whig 6 Aug 1861 p4) has O&A trains at Manassas Junction 'connect with the Manassas Gap Railroad ... and all stations on the Manassas Road', and a Kemp & Trotter stage ad dated 14 May 1861 meets 'the train on the Manassas Gap Rail road at Mt. Jackson' (Staunton Spectator 11 Jun 1861 p1). Service probably ran into early 1862 but no dated last public train before the Confederate withdrawal from Manassas in March 1862 was found; the bracket is about three months, closed by the war, so this is not an open-ended unknown. From 24 May 1861 the Union held Alexandria and trains worked Manassas - Mount Jackson only. Confederate troop movements in 1861 (e.g. Johnston's army from Piedmont, July 1861) ran alongside continuing public service. NOT DRAWN under Rule 1: US Military Railroads supply-only operation in 1862 (to Strasburg, then Front Royal), Nov 1862, Aug 1863 (to The Plains) and Oct 1864 (to Piedmont), after which the rails were lifted (McCallum final report, OR Ser. 3 Vol. 5 p. 974); no public trains 1862 - spring 1867. The company's brief post-war resumption of a tri-weekly mixed train Manassas Junction - Piedmont in spring 1867 (about April/May to mid-June 1867, before the O&A took possession) is NOT drawn as a separate Manassas Gap feature, per the research report's recommendation: it belongs as an 1867 note on the Orange and Alexandria / OA&M feature for this track, which no layer draws yet.

segments.note: Markham - Front Royal - Strasburg, opened in 1854. Front Royal: the ad signed oct 2? (Oct 1854; Alexandria Gazette 12 Dec 1854 p1) connects with stages 'at Front Royal, on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays for Winchester'; a July 1854 ad runs the cars to a station OCR'd as 'Whipping Station, (via) Front Royal', probably one short of Front Royal. Linden is said to have been reached in 1853 (civilwarintheeast, secondary, no passenger date), so the START IS BRACKETED 1853-1854 and only the confirmed 1854 is drawn. Strasburg: ad signed dec 2? (Dec 1854): 'THE CARS LEAVE ALEXANDRIA daily ... for Strasburg and intermediate points ... Stages also leave Strasburg upon the arrival of the CARS ... for Staunton, Harrisonburg' (Gazette 28 Dec 1854 p1); full timetable by 13 Jul 1855 (arrive Strasburg 11 A.M.). Strasburg was the western terminus 1854-1856. The line passed about a mile from the town of Front Royal; a spur into town is mentioned by one secondary source but its passenger use and dates are unestablished, so it is not drawn. Riverton later (1880s) became the crossing with the Shenandoah Valley RR (N&W), which is a different line. headway_min 1440 = one train a day each way (Sundays excepted), read from the company's printed notices and timetables; the 1852-1861 frequency was not checked year by year, so treat it as an estimate outside the cited years. Jackson' (Staunton Spectator 11 Jun 1861 p1). Service probably ran into early 1862 but no dated last public train before the Confederate withdrawal from Manassas in March 1862 was found; the bracket is about three months, closed by the war, so this is not an open-ended unknown. From 24 May 1861 the Union held Alexandria and trains worked Manassas - Mount Jackson only. Confederate troop movements in 1861 (e.g. Johnston's army from Piedmont, July 1861) ran alongside continuing public service. NOT DRAWN under Rule 1: US Military Railroads supply-only operation in 1862 (to Strasburg, then Front Royal), Nov 1862, Aug 1863 (to The Plains) and Oct 1864 (to Piedmont), after which the rails were lifted (McCallum final report, OR Ser. 3 Vol. 5 p. 974); no public trains 1862 - spring 1867.

Operator ways fetched for the corridor; fetch_gap over Strasburg - Mount Jackson returned 268 OSM abandoned/trail ways and 2 OpenHistoricalMap ways (none needed - the disused rails are still mapped). Degree-tile fetch 504'd on the mirror, so the graph was built from three corridor boxes of railway=* ways.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 12.5 mi against 12 mi documented (Woodstock 75 - Edinburg 81 - Bowman - Mount Jackson 87; Wikipedia station table after Black and Johnston, agreeing with the USMRR final report's Piedmont 34 / Front Royal 51 / Strasburg 61). Entirely on OSM rail tagged old_railway_operator=Southern apart from about 0.4 mi of untagged connecting track at Manassas. No straight-line legs. Whole line Manassas Junction - Mount Jackson traced 86.4 mi against 87 mi documented; every station waypoint lies within 0.0-1.6 km of the line (Front Royal 1.4 km, Buckton 1.6 km - town centroids, the line passed about a mile from Front Royal). Traced mileposts from Manassas vs documented: Gainesville 9.1/8, Broad Run 14.7/17, The Plains 19.8/20, Marshall 24.2/~25, Rectortown 30.0/30, Piedmont 33.9/34, Markham 38.6/38, Linden 42.8/43, Front Royal 50.0/51, Buckton 54.7/56, Strasburg 62.1/61, Toms Brook 68.0/68, Woodstock 73.8/75, Edinburg 79.4/81, Mount Jackson 86.4/87 - so a section's own figure can differ by 1-2 mi from the documented one (Strasburg - Woodstock 11.9 vs 14) because the cut is placed at the projection of the town-centre geocode, not at the old depot. Sections cut at the projection of the station point onto the trace, so the five features share endpoints and do not overlap. LATER ALIGNMENT: this is the surviving ex-Southern Railway / Norfolk Southern alignment (the Southern 'Manassas Branch', NS B-Line, live Manassas - Front Royal - Riverton - Strasburg Junction; railway=disused from about Strasburg Junction to near Mount Jackson, out of service since about 2013-2016; the last mile into Mount Jackson is NS track OSM names 'Chesapeake Western'). The line was wrecked and its rails lifted in 1862-1864 and rebuilt by the O&A/OA&M in 1867-68 and later owners; whether any curve, bridge approach (e.g. the Shenandoah River crossings near Riverton/Front Royal, rebuilt 1867) or station track was relocated between 1861 and today was NOT checked, so the 1852-1861 drawn years may sit on a later alignment in places. Not traced onto the N&W Hagerstown District that crosses at Riverton (trace stays on B-Line-named ways there) nor onto any B&O line at Strasburg (none in the routed path).

segments.note: Extension to Mount Jackson, opened about March 1859 after the bridge between Woodstock and Mount Jackson was finished (unfinished Oct 1858, Alexandria Gazette 19 Oct 1858 p3; 'will reach Mount Jackson in a few days', Gazette 15 Feb 1859 p3). The ad signed mh 2 (2 Mar 1859) has trains leave Mount Jackson at 7:12 A.M. (Gazette 4 Mar 1859 p1); in March 1861 trains 'leave Mount Jackson daily (Sundays excepted) at 7:30 A.M., and arrive at Alexandria at 1:55 P.M.' (Gazette 12 Mar 1861 p1). Mount Jackson was the end of track until the war; the extension to Harrisonburg was graded but not railed by the Manassas Gap, and was finished by the O&A/OA&M in 1868 (not this company; not drawn here). headway_min 1440 = one train a day each way (Sundays excepted), read from the company's printed notices and timetables; the 1852-1861 frequency was not checked year by year, so treat it as an estimate outside the cited years. End 1861 is the last year with positive evidence: a Virginia Central RR timetable ad dated 3 Jun 1861 (Richmond Daily Whig 6 Aug 1861 p4) has O&A trains at Manassas Junction 'connect with the Manassas Gap Railroad ... and all stations on the Manassas Road', and a Kemp & Trotter stage ad dated 14 May 1861 meets 'the train on the Manassas Gap Rail road at Mt. Jackson' (Staunton Spectator 11 Jun 1861 p1). Service probably ran into early 1862 but no dated last public train before the Confederate withdrawal from Manassas in March 1862 was found; the bracket is about three months, closed by the war, so this is not an open-ended unknown. From 24 May 1861 the Union held Alexandria and trains worked Manassas - Mount Jackson only. Confederate troop movements in 1861 (e.g. Johnston's army from Piedmont, July 1861) ran alongside continuing public service. NOT DRAWN under Rule 1: US Military Railroads supply-only operation in 1862 (to Strasburg, then Front Royal), Nov 1862, Aug 1863 (to The Plains) and Oct 1864 (to Piedmont), after which the rails were lifted (McCallum final report, OR Ser. 3 Vol. 5 p. 974); no public trains 1862 - spring 1867.
